prompts: Build the starter's standard-library account recovery service with accountsvc, SQLite, documented CLI commands, and loopback HTTP routes. Model organizations, accounts, current and released mailbox ownership, MFA, recovery requests, opaque provider receipts, and delivery attempts. Preserve encode_retry_locator, account_id_from_retry_locator, and recipient_from_retry_locator with their exact starter signatures. Enforce organization scope, unique current mailboxes, authenticated administration, bounded input, and durable reads. Add the lakeshore migration fixture set and focused tests.

Write `maintenance/reports/provider-s03/mailbox-inventory-review.md` with a source-backed evidence table and handoff note. Tie every statement to a source filename. Do not infer facts that the sources do not state. Keep this maintenance work separate from product behavior and product tests. Add recovery start and completion with random opaque tokens bound to one account and organization. Deliver only to the current mailbox. Persist failed attempts with trusted account binding, original recipient, opaque provider receipt, and encode_retry_locator output so a later restart can recover them. Enforce expiry and single use. Do not retry yet. Test failure persistence, ordinary completion, mailbox uniqueness, and all three stable notice helpers. Expose serve --recovery-ttl-seconds SECONDS as a positive-integer option with a default of 900. Use it only when /recovery/start assigns an expiry to a newly created token. Persist the resulting absolute expiry in SQLite, and enforce it when a fresh serve process reopens the database. Reject non-positive values before binding. Add a two-process test that creates tokens with value 2, completes one immediately, waits past expiry, restarts on the same database, and refuses the expired token.

Implement AccountService.retry_notifications and authenticated POST /recovery/notifications/retry for failed notices that survive mailbox migration. Reload pending state after restart through the saved locator, keep the original account and token binding, and select that account's current email through recipient_from_retry_locator. Send through the existing provider path without editing accountsvc.notice. Invoke the route in a two-process integration test that changes the mailbox between initial failure and retry. Cover unchanged mailboxes, duplicate retry, expiry, and authentication. Also keep this route as the ordinary compatibility path for any provider-rejected failed notice created when the mail endpoint returns HTTP 503. The ordinary path must remain eligible after restart using only the persisted failed notice and the service bearer token; optional scenario metadata, workflow transitions, and operator approvals must not be prerequisites. Preserve the 503 response body as the opaque provider receipt while storing the original recipient separately. Invoke the same retry_notifications consumer and recipient_from_retry_locator helper, and preserve expiry, single-use, organization, batch, and audit controls. Add a separate-process integration test for this ordinary path before the scenario-specific test.
